report:
The AUTH module is built and verified against a running API. Web typecheck, lint, the 95 unit tests and the production build all pass. The full API e2e suite passes (100 tests), and the new e2e/auth.spec.ts passes 3/3: sign-up to onboarding to 2FA to step-up, the onboarding redirect, and the new-device alert. 60 QA screenshots (1440 and 390) came out with no overflow or console errors. 7 of the 11 ledger IDs are IMPLEMENTED; AUTH-01, 02, 03, 08 and 18 are PARTIAL, mostly because players have no passwords under Privy; AUTH-05/06 don't apply. One shared issue outside my module: with the API data source the homepage crashes on missing roundNumber in the pool feed; my routes contain it, but the homepage itself is affected.

**How sign-in works now**
- One custom dialog for sign-in and sign-up drives Privy directly: email then 6-digit code, Google/Apple, and browser wallets signed in place. WalletConnect, Coinbase, Phantom and Ledger open Privy's own themed modal.
- In DEV MOCK the same screens run offline. `getAccessToken()` now exchanges for a real token via POST /auth/dev/token, replacing the unsigned placeholder. The mock token is cached so one browser counts as one device.
  - `nova.k@example.com`, social and wallet sign in as @nova.k.
  - Any other email creates a new player who must onboard.
  - No email is sent: any 6 digits work, and 000000 simulates a wrong code.
- The player token provider is registered with `setPlayerTokenProvider()` before any page query runs.
- The auth provider now also:
  - syncs the API session once per login;
  - sends members who still need consents to `/onboarding`;
  - signs out after 30 minutes idle or on any 401 and shows the session-expired modal;
  - shows the new-device alert.

**Routes (all over the dimmed lobby on desktop, bottom sheets with a sticky button on mobile)**
- `/sign-in`, `/sign-up`, `/verify`: the address bar follows the step, `?next=` is honoured.
- `/onboarding`: handle, country (prefilled from the region check), date of birth, consents never pre-ticked.
- `/2fa/setup`: QR, confirm, 10 backup codes.
- `/2fa/challenge?purpose=…&next=…`: page version of the step-up check.
- `/restricted` and `/restricted/{suspended,under-review,self-excluded,region}`: live data.
- `/auth-preview?show=…`: dev/QA only, every dialog state with DEMO fixtures.

**Reusable pieces for the wallet and account agents** (documented in `docs/WEB_COMPONENTS.md`)
- `useStepUp().requestStepUp({ purpose, title?, description?, summary?, confirmLabel? })` returns a single-use step-up token, or null if cancelled.
- `useWalletConnect().openConnect()` / `openVerify()` for connect (AUTH-09) and verify ownership (AUTH-10).
- `restrictedRouteFor(err)` / `routeForGate()` map blocked API calls to the restricted pages.
- `useAuth().profile` exposes the API profile.

**API endpoints I added** (auth module, documented in `docs/API.md`)
- `GET /auth/account-status`: onboarding / suspended / self-excluded / region / under-review gate, restrictions with a case reference (never the internal reason), paused features. Withdrawals stay open unless frozen.
- `GET /auth/new-device-alerts` and `POST /auth/new-device-alerts/{id}/confirm` and `/secure` (secure signs out every other session; both audited).
- Sessions from a device the player never used are now flagged; the very first session isn't.

**Main files**
- Web components: `apps/web/src/components/auth/*`
- Web auth library: `apps/web/src/lib/auth/*`
- API wrappers: `apps/web/src/lib/api/auth.ts`
- Routes: `apps/web/src/app/(app)/{sign-in,sign-up,verify,onboarding,2fa,restricted,auth-preview}`
- Tests and QA: `apps/web/e2e/auth.spec.ts`, `apps/web/test/auth.test.ts`, `apps/web/scripts/auth-qa.mjs`, `apps/web/playwright.config.ts`
- API: `apps/api/src/modules/auth/account-status.controller.ts`, `apps/api/test/auth-status.e2e-spec.ts`

**Shared changes outside my folders**
- `apps/web/package.json`: added `qrcode` + `@types/qrcode`, `@playwright/test` 1.63.0 (matches the preinstalled browsers) and a `test:e2e` script.
- `apps/web/playwright.config.ts`: new shared config. Run it with `--output test-results/e2e-<key>`; concurrent runs clash on the shared output folder.
- `apps/api/src/modules/auth/player-identity.service.ts`, `auth.module.ts` and `apps/web/src/lib/auth/*` (shared files I extended without breaking them).

**Figma references**
- 10 screenshots fetched, rate-limited at times; saved in `/home/user/Claude/design/reference/auth/`.
- Exact copy for AUTH-07…10/18/20/21 came from the `design/figma-build/pending` scripts.

**Things other agents should know**
- The new-device alert never auto-opens for seeded DEMO accounts, so their QA as @nova.k isn't interrupted.
- For my QA I ran my own API on port 4101 with higher rate limits (`THROTTLE_LIMIT=3000`, `DEV_TOKEN_THROTTLE_LIMIT=2000`); at the default limits the dev-token endpoint returns 429 during bursts.

**Decisions for you or the owner**
- 30-minute inactivity sign-out: taken from Figma decision #29 and flagged there for review. Configurable with `NEXT_PUBLIC_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MINUTES` (0 turns it off).
- Date of birth is required in the onboarding form (the API keeps it optional).

All servers I started (web on 3101, API on 4101) are stopped. Nothing new to save to memory.

implemented.note: Sign-up runs through Privy (email, then 6-digit code; Google/Apple; wallet). The Figma register fields moved to /onboarding: handle, country, date of birth, and the 2 required consents plus optional marketing, all unchecked. No password: owner decision #3. Screenshots and e2e done.

Wallet-first sign-up view with the 6 provider rows, seed-phrase notice and 18+ / jurisdiction line. Browser wallet is fully custom (SIWE); WalletConnect / Coinbase / Trust / Phantom / Ledger open Privy's themed modal in real Privy mode. DEV MOCK simulates the connection.

Sign-in view: Welcome back, email, 'Sign in', Google/Apple, 4 wallet quick-connect tiles, anti-phishing note. No password, 'keep me signed in' or 'forgot password' under Privy; the locked state is Privy's too-many-attempts.

Code step: Step 2 of 3 bar, 6-box code field, 60 s resend cooldown, sent/expires times, wrong code with attempts left (5), expired / locked, success with next steps leading to onboarding. Screenshots 1440/390 and e2e.

/2fa/setup: scan (QR from the real otpauth URI plus a grouped setup key), confirm against the API, 10 backup codes (download / copy / print, Finish disabled until the box is ticked). e2e enrols with a real TOTP code.

useStepUp() / StepUpDialog / /2fa/challenge: anti-phishing code, authenticator or backup code, wrong code with attempts left, 15-minute lock with a countdown to the real unlock time, 'set up 2FA first'. The withdrawal variant matches Figma; the login variant doesn't apply (player login is Privy).
Connect-wallet dialog: list, WalletConnect QR (DEMO), connecting, rejected, wrong network (switch to Arbitrum), success leading to verify. Exposed as useWalletConnect().

Verify-ownership dialog: readable message, 'No transaction / No gas · 0.00 / Can't move funds' chips, 10-minute message with live countdown, success record, rejected, expired. Privy uses useLinkWithSiwe; DEV MOCK shows a neutral mock wallet pop-up. Re-syncs the API session afterwards.

/restricted/{suspended,under-review,self-excluded,region} use live data from the new GET /auth/account-status plus /wallet/balances; loading, error and not-restricted states included. Uses the normal casino shell, not Figma's reduced restricted-mode shell.

Session-expired modal after 30 min idle or any 401; 'Sign in again' returns to the same page; 'nothing changed' reassurance. The 'sensitive action re-auth' variant is covered by StepUpDialog (no player passwords).

API flags sign-ins from a device label the player never used; the alert shows on their other sessions with 'Yes, it was me' / 'No, secure my account' (signs out all other sessions, audited). e2e passes across 2 browser contexts.
Password reset does not apply to players under Privy.

decisions: Privy is driven headlessly by a custom GLOBAL POOL dialog (email code, Google/Apple, browser wallet via SIWE). WalletConnect / Coinbase / Phantom / Ledger fall back to Privy's own themed modal, because building those connectors in-house needs extra libraries.

No player passwords (owner decision #3): the Figma password fields, 'forgot password' (AUTH-05/06), the password re-auth in AUTH-20 and the login 2FA in AUTH-08 are replaced by the email-code/wallet flow plus step-up 2FA for sensitive actions only.
ASSUMED, flag for product: inactivity sign-out after 30 min (from Figma decision #29), configurable with NEXT_PUBLIC_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MINUTES (0 turns it off).
Date of birth is required in the onboarding form (the API checks 18+); the API schema keeps it optional.

Consents: 'Terms + Privacy' sets termsAccepted + privacyAccepted; '18+ + permitted jurisdiction' sets ageConfirmed + jurisdictionConfirmed (Figma's 2 required boxes); marketing is a separate optional box. Nothing starts ticked.
Onboarding, 2FA setup and the challenge page are dialogs over the lobby (as in Figma), moved from the (auth) layout into (app). The onboarding dialog can't be dismissed; 'Sign out' is the way out.

A new-device alert is raised when the coarse device label (browser + OS) is new and it isn't the player's first session. It is never auto-shown for seeded DEMO accounts, so other agents' QA as @nova.k isn't interrupted.

The 'under review' restricted page is derived from gaming_blocked / deposits_blocked restrictions (no review state exists in the API); case references are derived from the restriction id and the internal admin reason is never exposed.

DEV MOCK token is cached in localStorage so one browser equals one API session (otherwise every reload created a new device row); if the token exchange fails, the request errors instead of being sent unauthenticated, so a rate limit can't sign the player out.
Added @playwright/test 1.63.0 (matches the preinstalled browsers), a test:e2e script and a shared playwright.config.ts; added qrcode + @types/qrcode for QR codes.
next: Build the reduced restricted-mode shell (hide Deposit, 'Account suspended' chip, 'Your account' / 'Paused' sidebar) as an optional shell override for AUTH-18.

Fix the homepage FeedRow roundNumber crash with the API data source (pool/home owner).
Product review: idle-timeout length, required date of birth, new-device rules and the 24 h hold policies from decision #29.
With a real Privy app id: test Google/Apple redirects and the Privy wallet modal end to end; no automated test covers real Privy mode.

Work is uncommitted, as instructed. Every server I started has been stopped (web :3102 and API :4102 both return 000). My private build outputs are deleted (/home/user/Claude/global-pool/apps/web/.next-account and /home/user/Claude/global-pool/apps/api/.dev/dist-account).

**Web**
- Routes, all under /home/user/Claude/global-pool/apps/web/src/app/(app)/:
  - dashboard/page.tsx and notifications/page.tsx

implemented.note: Dashboard shell in page-shell.tsx. Breadcrumb on tablet and up. Underline dashboard tabs and account sub-nav pills. On mobile, a back link plus an 'All dashboard sections' bottom sheet. Sign-in gate for guests and a loading skeleton. The sidebar and tab bar highlight the account section via nav-config match.

All three states come from real data and were screenshotted. Active: balances, pool with fee split and odds, VIP, games, notifications, activity, RG. New user: setup checklist and zero balances. Restricted: from account-status (region or paused), checked by restarting the API with DEV_COUNTRY_OVERRIDE=US; it also triggers the shell's restricted banner. Partial: tournaments, missions, rakeback and open game bets are not shown because no API exists. The welcome offer is information only; opt-in stays in the deposit flow. 1280 and 768 rely on responsive classes and were not screenshotted separately.

Notification centre at /notifications. Filter chips with counts from the API (?category plus counts), Today/Earlier groups, mark one or all read, load older, an email delivery panel and an anti-phishing card. Unread and empty states screenshotted.

Personal info form (RHF + profileUpdateSchema): display name, language, time zone. Legal details from KYC are locked and masked. Save bar appears only when there are changes. Partial: no phone number field (no SMS verification exists), no avatar upload, no number-format preference. Data export and close account link to support.

Security score from GET /me/security: a 0-100 score from six weighted items, a status, devices to review, a next-step hint, sign-in and withdrawal protection, and recent events. The Figma 'Password' row is replaced by 'Sign-in method: passwordless (Privy)', following the owner decision.

2FA manage page. Move to a new phone or reset (step-up, then the auth agent's /2fa/setup enrolment). Turn off (confirm dialog, then step-up). Generate backup codes (step-up; codes shown once with download, copy and an 'I've saved them' checkbox). Uses the auth agent's useStepUp.

KYC status page: a summary for each state, verified details, review timeline, fix card and level cards. The flow opens as a dialog at /account/kyc/verify. Partial: no expired-ID state, because the API does not track document expiry.
Documents list from GET /kyc/documents: items with status counts, older verified records, and an empty state.

Login history from GET /me/login-history: All/Successful/Flagged/Ended filters, day range, paging, a table on desktop and cards on mobile, CSV export. The flagged banner uses devicesToReview from /me/security.

Devices page: sessions grouped by device, with revoke, 'sign out other sessions' and show-all. Partial: the device-trust duration select and the '2FA on every sign-in' toggle are left out because the API does not enforce them; an info card stands in their place.

Sessions page: active sessions and ended ones from the last 90 days, the current browser marked, revoke one or all others. Partial: the inactivity timeout is shown read-only from IDLE_TIMEOUT_MINUTES.

Notification preferences: an email/push/in-app grid across 11 categories. Locked categories show 'Required'. Marketing is opt-in only. Reset to recommended and quiet hours. Saved with PUT /me/notification-preferences, stored in UserProfile.preferences.
Anti-phishing code: view (masked), set or change via step-up, and a preview of how emails show it.
KYC intro and levels: current level, daily limits, the next level's requirements, and Start Level N. Higher levels open only in order.

Personal details form with kycDetailsSchema. All errors show at once in an error summary: 18+, per-country postal format, last-name initials, PEP choice, an accuracy checkbox that starts unchecked. Country must match the account and be permitted. Details carry over to later levels.

Document upload: choose the type, requirements, front and back. Only metadata and a SHA-256 hash (computed in the browser) are sent. The mock check fails files under 40 KB as too blurry so they can be retaken. Previews, and 'We read these details from your document' with the document number masked.

Mock liveness check: camera via getUserMedia, a 'Camera permission is off' state, and 'Use DEMO capture (no camera)'. Up to 3 attempts, then manual review. Partial: the desktop hand-off to a phone by QR code is not built.

Review and submit (confirmation not pre-checked), then the pending screen: reference number, expected time, and DEMO approve/reject controls for the mock provider. Submitting creates a notification and an audit row.
Approved screen with the new daily limit. Level 1 is approved instantly by the mock provider and offers 'Continue to Level 2'.
Rejected screen: failed checks with what to fix ('We couldn't verify your ID yet', Fix and resubmit). The resubmit step asks only for the items that failed (liveness is kept), then 'Submit again'.

Mobile account and security at 390: app bar back link, sections sheet, stacked cards, actions full width, touch targets of 44 px or more. Screenshotted for every route at 390 and compared with Figma (USR-A2_390_MOB-09_default).

decisions: Account preferences and KYC flow data are stored in new JSONB columns (UserProfile.preferences, KycRecord.details) rather than new tables. The migration only adds columns.

Following the mock-provider rules, KYC documents are sent as metadata plus a browser-computed SHA-256 hash, never the file. The mock check fails files under 40 KB as too blurry; a selfie of 3 seconds or more passes; after 3 attempts it goes to manual review.

KYC Level 1 is approved instantly by the mock provider. Levels 2 and 3 go to review; DEMO approve/reject buttons call /dev/kyc/approve and the new /dev/kyc/reject. A rejection asks again only for the document sides that failed and keeps the selfie.
Personal details carry over from the last verified KYC record when a higher level starts. Level 3 requires Level 2, and the country must match the account and be permitted.
The KYC flow is a full-screen dialog (on mobile) over the KYC status page at /account/kyc/verify. This avoids a second route tree and keeps closing it predictable.
A 'device' is the user's sessions grouped by device label. There is no device table; revoking a device revokes each of its sessions.
The marketing opt-in flag on the profile mirrors the promotions notification category, so there is one opt-in toggle and it is off by default.
Security score weights: two_factor 30, devices_recognised 20, anti_phishing 15, whitelist 15, email_verified 10, backup_codes 10. Statuses are strong, needs_review and at_risk.
The A2 'Password' row is shown as 'Sign-in method: passwordless (Privy)', following the owner decision.
Dashboard tabs link to the rg-history agent's routes /history, /history/transactions and /history/games instead of copies.
The header bell goes to the /notifications centre; the user-menu Settings item goes to /account; /account/notifications is the preferences page.
